hook: Tim O'Reilly built O'Reilly Media from a technical writing business into a publisher of programming books and an organiser of technology conferences. His company hosted the 1998 summit at which free software leaders adopted the term open source, and its 2004 Web 2.0 Conference popularised the label for the web that emerged after the dot-com crash. In recent years his writing has turned to the economics of platforms, including research on how algorithms steer user attention.

quick_facts: Founder and CEO of O'Reilly Media, according to his biography on the company's site, retrieved in October 2026.
Born in Cork, Ireland, in 1954, he grew up in San Francisco and studied classics at Harvard College.
In 1992 his company published The Whole Internet User's Guide and Catalog, and in 1993 it launched the Global Network Navigator, an early commercial web portal that AOL bought in 1995.
He received InfoWorld's Industry Achievement Award in 1999 for his advocacy of open source.
In 2006 he started the early-stage venture firm O'Reilly AlphaTech Ventures with Mark Jacobsen and Bryce Roberts.
He joined the board of Code for America in 2010 and has held a visiting professorship of practice at University College London.

achievements.title: The 1998 open source summit
achievements.impact: O'Reilly & Associates hosted the April 1998 meeting, first announced as a Freeware Summit, at which free software leaders adopted open source, a term proposed weeks earlier by Christine Peterson. Peterson credits O'Reilly and Eric Raymond with persuading the wider community to use it.

achievements.title: Web 2.0 Conference (2004)
achievements.impact: Co-hosted with John Battelle and MediaLive, the conference popularised Web 2.0 as the name for the participatory web that followed the dot-com crash, although the phrase had appeared in a 1999 article by Darcy DiNucci.

achievements.title: Global Network Navigator (1993)
achievements.impact: His company's GNN was among the first commercial sites on the web and was sold to AOL in 1995.

achievements.title: Algorithmic attention rents (2024)
achievements.impact: With Ilan Strauss and Mariana Mazzucato, argued in Data and Policy that dominant platforms can use their algorithms to steer users toward results that benefit the platform, and urged regulators to require disclosure of how platforms allocate attention.

source_basis: This profile was written mainly from the Wikipedia article on Tim O'Reilly, retrieved 2026-10-22, with awards, dates and current role checked against his biography and timeline on oreilly.com, the 2024 Data and Policy paper and Christine Peterson's account of the 1998 summit.
